fields.why: Q3 2016 to Q3 2017 percent changes are reported and ranked across 6 county urbanization levels ('highest ... in large central metropolitan') and across 4 age groups.
Age is clear. Urbanization is a county classification (facility or residence county is not stated); reading it as rurality is defensible, though it could be argued to be geography of non-human units.

The chi-square tests and joinpoint QPC p-values each test a period change within one urbanization or age level (rule 6: a non-SPD contrast within SPD levels), so no test runs across the groups; the flag is a false hit.

brief_issues: Rule on 'rurality of non-human units' does not say whether NCHS county urbanization of where ED visits occurred counts as rurality; a rule naming county urban-rural schemes applied to person-level events as rurality would decide it.
